extracted.intended_audience: People of the State of New York; citizens/voters weighing ratification of the proposed Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: A sequence of Federalist Papers (Nos. XI–XV) arguing for the benefits of a general Union of the states, especially for commerce, revenue, economy in government, and the practicability of a large republic under representative institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of naval protection to commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The necessity of naval protection to external or maritime commerce does not require a particular elucidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naval protection is implicitly essential because maritime commerce is vital to national prosperity; a navy safeguards external commerce and therefore warrants political attention and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of government promotes commercial prosperity
rubrics_metrics.description: A unity of commercial, as well as political, interests, can only result from a unity of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unrestrained intercourse between States advances trade by interchange of productions, increases variety and stability of exportable goods, reduces risk of stagnation from fluctuations in demand, and makes the aggregate balance of commerce more favorable than that of disunited States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union reduces obstacles to trade and competition increases favorable terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial enterprise will have much greater scope, from the diversity in the productions of different States... It can be conducted upon much better terms with a large number of materials of a given value than with a small number of materials of the same value; arising from the competitions of trade and from the fluctuations of markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A larger, unified market yields competitive advantages, reduces vulnerability to localized crop failures or demand shifts, and supports speculative and sustained commercial operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union enables a stronger, independent national standing against European influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the thirteen States, bound together in a strict and indissoluble Union, concur in erecting one great American system, superior to the control of all transatlantic force or influence, and able to dictate the terms of the connection between the old and the new world!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political unity is presented as necessary for resisting foreign domination and for vindicating national honor and independence in international affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce is the primary and most productive source of national wealth and revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosperity of commerce ... has become a primary object of their political cares. By multiplying the means of gratification, by promoting the introduction and circulation of the precious metals ... it serves to vivify and invigorate the channels of industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because commerce increases money in circulation and its velocity, it directly augments a country's ability to pay taxes; therefore public policy should favor commercial growth to secure revenue and economic health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence on indirect taxes (duties) rather than direct taxation in America
rubrics_metrics.description: In America, it is evident that we must a long time depend for the means of revenue chiefly on such duties. In most parts of it, excises must be confined within a narrow compass. The genius of the people will ill brook the inquisitive and peremptory spirit of excise laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical and cultural constraints make excises and direct taxes less viable in the United States; thus imposts and duties on imports should be relied upon as the principal revenue source.

rubrics_metrics.name: A single national government simplifies collection and enforcement of customs duties
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on the contrary, there be but one government pervading all the States, there will be, as to the principal part of our commerce, but ONE SIDE to guard—the ATLANTIC COAST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national government can concentrate enforcement on coastal entries, render duties more productive with ordinary vigilance and fewer armed vessels, and avoid the inland evasion and circuitous contraband trade that separate governments would encourage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disunion would increase illicit trade and make collection of revenue more costly
rubrics_metrics.description: The separate States or confederacies would be necessitated by mutual jealousy to avoid the temptations to that kind of trade by the lowness of their duties... a circuitous contraband to one State, through the medium of another, would be both easy and safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragmentation would create incentives for low duties, smuggling, and complex enforcement needs (e.g., large patrol forces), making revenue collection less effective and more expensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union permits higher and more productive duties with less prejudice to trade
rubrics_metrics.description: It is therefore evident, that one national government would be able, at much less expense, to extend the duties on imports, beyond comparison, further than would be practicable to the States separately...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A unified enforcement regime and larger market make it feasible to raise import duties (example: ardent spirits) to levels that would be productive of substantial revenue without unduly harming commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of governance through a single civil list and avoidance of duplicate establishments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the States are united under one government, there will be but one national civil list to support; if they are divided into several confederacies, there will be as many different national civil lists to be provided for...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Union saves administrative expense by preventing multiplicity of national civil lists, duplicate continental guard forces, and multiple military establishments that would otherwise arise from jealousies between separate states or confederacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: A republic can be extensive if founded on representation (distinguish republic vs. democracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true distinction between these forms was also adverted to ... in a democracy, the people meet and exercise the government in person; in a republic, they assemble and administer it by their representatives and agents. A democracy ... will be confined to a small spot. A republic may be extended over a large region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practicability objection to an extensive republic is rebutted by noting representative institutions allow large territories to be governed effectively; examples cited include German and Polish diets and the British parliamentary system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal government limited to enumerated objects; state governments retain separate authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The general government is not to be charged with the whole power of making and administering laws. Its jurisdiction is limited to certain enumerated objects... The subordinate governments... will retain their due authority and activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical governance in an extensive union depends on dividing powers: the national government handles common concerns while states manage local affairs, preserving practicability and local responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frontier states will have particular incentives to support and benefit from Union
rubrics_metrics.description: As almost every State will, on one side or other, be a frontier... the States which lie at the greatest distance from the heart of the Union... will be at the same time immediately contiguous to foreign nations, and will consequently stand, on particular occasions, in greatest need of its strength and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if distant states receive fewer everyday benefits from a centralized government, their frontier exposure makes Union particularly valuable for defense and support, maintaining an overall equilibrium of advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: The present Confederation is insufficient to preserve the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: There is scarcely anything that can wound the pride or degrade the character of an independent nation which we do not experience... debts ... remain without any proper or satisfactory provision for their discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material defects of the Articles of Confederation (inability to meet engagements, raise revenues, or secure posts) are presented as empirical evidence necessitating a stronger national government.
